widgetTypes.description: A single KPI tile — a value with an optional delta.

fields.doc: Dot-path into the run output payload, e.g. "totals.revenue".
Optional dot-path to a delta/comparison value shown alongside the metric.
Display format. "currency" is USD; "percent" expects a 0-1 fraction.
Suffix appended to a "number"-formatted value, e.g. "kg".

widgetTypes.tomlExample:
[[widgets]]
type = "metric"
id = "revenue"
title = "Total revenue"
value_key = "totals.revenue"
format = "currency"

widgetTypes.description: Several KPI tiles in one horizontal row — for a handful of related numbers that read better side by side than as separate `metric` widgets competing for grid columns.

fields.doc: One or more `{ label, value_key, delta_key?, format?, unit? }` entries — each is the same value/delta/format/unit contract as a `metric` widget, rendered as one tile in the row.

widgetTypes.tomlExample:
[[widgets]]
type = "kpi-rail"
id = "summary"
title = "Run summary"
items = [
  { label = "Total cost", value_key = "totals.cost", format = "currency" },
  { label = "Makespan", value_key = "totals.makespan", unit = "min" },
  { label = "Utilization", value_key = "totals.utilization", format = "percent" },
]

widgetTypes.description: A sortable data grid bound to an array of row objects.

fields.doc: Dot-path to an array of row objects in the run output payload.
One or more `{ key, label? }` entries, in display order. `key` is a top-level field on each row (not a dot-path).

widgetTypes.tomlExample:
[[widgets]]
type = "table"
id = "breakdown"
title = "Breakdown"
rows_key = "breakdown"
columns = [
  { key = "name", label = "Name" },
  { key = "value", label = "Value" },
]

widgetTypes.description: Shows the fields of whichever row is currently selected (via a `timeline` click, or any other selecting view) — looked up by matching `id_key` against the selection id.

fields.doc: Dot-path to the array of row objects a selection is looked up in.
Row field compared against the current selection id — the same field the selecting view (e.g. `timeline`'s `id_key`) used to identify that row.
Which row fields to show, and in what order/label. Omit to show every field on the matched row.

widgetTypes.tomlExample:
[[widgets]]
type = "detail"
id = "task-detail"
title = "Task details"
items_key = "schedule"
id_key = "op"
fields = [
  { key = "task", label = "Task" },
  { key = "resource", label = "Machine" },
]

widgetTypes.description: A picker that sets the dashboard's selection — one option per distinct `id_key` value in `items_key`. An alternative to clicking a `timeline` bar, for choosing an item by name.

fields.doc: Dot-path to the array of row objects to pick options from.
Row field set as the selection id when an option is picked.
Row field shown as each option's label. Defaults to the id itself.

widgetTypes.tomlExample:
[[widgets]]
type = "filter"
id = "task-filter"
title = "Choose a task"
items_key = "schedule"
id_key = "op"
label_key = "task"

widgetTypes.description: A flat treemap — one rectangle per row, area proportional to `value_key`, labeled from `name_key`. Good for a breakdown where relative size matters more than exact values (e.g. cost by machine).

fields.doc: Dot-path to the array of row objects to size rectangles from.
Row field sized into each rectangle's area. Rows with a missing or non-positive value are dropped.
Row field shown as each rectangle's label.
Row field grouped into a stable color per distinct value. Omit for one palette color per rectangle in source order.

widgetTypes.tomlExample:
[[widgets]]
type = "treemap"
id = "cost-breakdown"
title = "Cost by machine"
items_key = "breakdown"
value_key = "cost"
name_key = "machine"

widgetTypes.description: A line chart — good for a value trending over time. Deprecated: prefer `chart` with `variant = "line"`; this type is kept only so dashboards written before `chart` existed keep rendering.

fields.doc: Dot-path to an array of data points in the run output payload.
The data point field to use as the category/x-axis value.
One or more `{ key, label?, color? }` entries — each renders as its own line/bar.

widgetTypes.tomlExample:
[[widgets]]
type = "line-chart"
id = "trend"
title = "Objective value over time"
data_key = "timeseries"
x_key = "label"
series = [{ key = "value", label = "Objective value" }]

widgetTypes.description: A bar chart — good for comparing values across categories. Deprecated: prefer `chart` with `variant = "bar"`; this type is kept only so dashboards written before `chart` existed keep rendering.

fields.doc: Dot-path to an array of data points in the run output payload.
The data point field to use as the category/x-axis value.
One or more `{ key, label?, color? }` entries — each renders as its own line/bar.

widgetTypes.tomlExample:
[[widgets]]
type = "bar-chart"
id = "breakdown-chart"
title = "Cost by warehouse"
data_key = "breakdown"
x_key = "name"
series = [{ key = "value", label = "Cost" }]

widgetTypes.description: A line or bar chart, picked by `variant` — folds `line-chart` and `bar-chart` into one type since they only ever differed in that. Use `variant = "line"` for a value trending over time, `"bar"` for comparing values across categories.

fields.doc: Which chart to draw: "line" for a trend, "bar" for comparing categories.
Dot-path to an array of data points in the run output payload.
The data point field to use as the category/x-axis value.
One or more `{ key, label?, color? }` entries — each renders as its own line/bar.

widgetTypes.tomlExample:
[[widgets]]
type = "chart"
id = "trend"
title = "Objective value over time"
variant = "line"
data_key = "timeseries"
x_key = "label"
series = [{ key = "value", label = "Objective value" }]

widgetTypes.description: A resource-row Gantt chart on a numeric time axis — the common shape for scheduling/job-shop solver results (one row per machine/resource, one bar per task).

fields.doc: Dot-path to an array of task objects in the run output payload.
Task field naming the resource/machine its row is grouped under. Defaults to "resource".
Task field for its display label. Defaults to "task".
Task field for its numeric start time. Defaults to "start".
Task field for its numeric end time. Set either this or `duration_key` — `end_key` wins when both are set, and a task resolving neither is dropped from the chart.
Task field for a numeric duration, added to `start_key`, for solvers that emit start+duration. Read only when `end_key` is unset.
Task field naming a categorical group (e.g. a job spanning several tasks), colored from a stable palette.
Suffix appended to axis tick labels and tooltip times, e.g. "min".

widgetTypes.tomlExample:
[[widgets]]
type = "gantt-chart"
id = "schedule"
title = "Machine schedule"
tasks_key = "schedule"
time_unit = "min"

widgetTypes.description: A resource-row timeline on a numeric time axis. Supersedes `gantt-chart`: interrupted work folds into one item drawn with gaps, non-working spans render as background bands, the axis is drag-to-zoom, a `[clock]` playhead shows as a now-marker, and rows it cannot draw are reported instead of silently dropped.

fields.doc: Dot-path to an array of interval objects in the run output payload.
Item field naming the resource/machine its row is grouped under. Defaults to "resource".
Item field for its display label. Defaults to "task".
Item field for its numeric start time. Defaults to "start".
Item field for its numeric end time. Set either this or `duration_key` — `end_key` wins when both are set.
Item field for a numeric duration, added to `start_key`, for solvers that emit start+duration. Read only when `end_key` is unset.
Item field naming a categorical group, colored from a stable palette.

Item field identifying the logical task a row belongs to. Rows sharing a value on one resource fold into a single interrupted item drawn with gaps, instead of separate bars that hide the fact they are one job.
Dot-path to an array of non-working spans (off-shift, maintenance), drawn as background bands.
Region field for its numeric start. Defaults to "start".
Region field for its numeric end. Defaults to "end".
Region field for a label shown on hover.
Region field naming the single resource it applies to. Regions without one apply to every row.
Suffix appended to axis tick labels and tooltip times, e.g. "min".

widgetTypes.tomlExample:
[[widgets]]
type = "timeline"
id = "schedule"
title = "Machine schedule"
items_key = "schedule"
id_key = "op"
regions_key = "breaks"
time_unit = "min"
